title: USGS Divide, Colo., 7.5-minute quadrangle, 1:24,000, 1954 (scan 232830)
holder: U.S. Geological Survey, Historical Topographic Map Collection
quote: OLD RAILROAD GRADE [Atlas note, not the source's words: The words are printed along a dashed line west of the stream from the highway south of Divide to Tracy Hill, where the line bends and runs south-east back to the highway near spot height 9289. The sheet also prints 'Well 9308' beside the grade, 'Tracy Hill', spot height 9396 on the highway, and 'Rule' along the stream (the rest of that name is outside the cut). It does not print Murphy. Five other 1954 scans of this sheet are listed by the USGS and were not looked at. Georeference checked against OpenStreetMap's Highway 67: within 3 to 10 m in three rows.]

title: 'Victorettes' (local notes), The Victor Record, 29 June 1900
holder: Colorado Historic Newspapers Collection (Colorado State Library)
quote: A Midland Terminal freight train was derailed at Murphy, the next station north of Gillett, about 5 o'clock yesterday morning. [Atlas note, not the source's words: Read from the collection's machine-read text, checked only as far as this sentence. 'Next station north of Gillett' does not agree with the later timetables, which put Midland and (in 1920 to 1933) Waters between Murphy and Gillett.]

title: 'Through the cab window', The Rocky Mountain News (Daily), 14 August 1901
holder: Colorado Historic Newspapers Collection (Colorado State Library)
quote: Midland Terminal train No. 10, leaving Cripple Creek 11:45 p. m., for Denver and the East ... was wrecked at Murphy, three miles south of Divide at 1:30 this morning by colliding with the rear end of an extra ore train [Atlas note, not the source's words: Dated Divide, 13 August. Machine-read text; the sentence quoted reads cleanly. The article says the flagman of the ore train 'failed to protect the rear end ... with signals', so the ore train was standing or slow at Murphy.]

title: 'Lightning and hailstones damage houses and stock', The Rocky Mountain News (Daily), 8 July 1907
holder: Colorado Historic Newspapers Collection (Colorado State Library)
quote: At Murphy, a small station on the Midland Terminal road, hailstones measuring almost two inches in diameter fell. [Atlas note, not the source's words: Dated Cripple Creek, 7 July. Machine-read text.]
